names.cache-aside: Redis cache in front of PostgreSQL
names.java-mixed: Spring Boot and PostgreSQL, mixed reads and writes
names.go-mixed: Go and PostgreSQL, mixed reads and writes
names.python-mixed: Flask on gunicorn and PostgreSQL, mixed reads and writes

notModelled.consumer: inside the model's queue node, which has no CPU or memory
notModelled.kafka: the model's queue node has no CPU or memory

noMemoryModel.postgres: the model has no database memory figure yet

measuredBy.window: each container's CPU and working set (memory less reclaimable page cache), read every {sampleSeconds} s inside the window k6 measures
measuredBy.scaled: each container's CPU over the whole k6 command, scaled to the measured window by the service's own CPU counter (these runs predate reading CPU inside the window; memory was not measured)
measuredBy.mixed: partly inside the measured window, partly scaled from the whole k6 command

kafka.text: Every Kafka run so far was measured with a broker healthcheck that started a Java tool every 3 s on the broker's own core (about half a core, all the time). Without it the same stack held the objective up to about 3,000 req/s in a trial on 31 Oct, so these measured knees are the benchmark's limit, not Kafka's. The healthcheck is fixed in compose.yaml; the next campaign measures Kafka again.
